pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

This PR contains several changes to allow users to fetch newly created dashboards and folders. 

The changes are:
* on client side: remove the use of authLib cache when running authZ service in-proc
* on server side: add a denial cache to return quickly when we know that a user does not have permission on a specific resource
* on server side: if permission denial cache is not hit, and the requested resource is not found in cached permissions, requery permissions from the DB

**Why do we need this feature?**

Otherwise dash/folder creator can't access the dashboard/folder that they've just created.

**Who is this feature for?**

Grafana users

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/identity-access-team/issues/1316
pr.title: AuthZService: improve authz caching

raw_findings.body: The render service (which `getRendererPermissions` always grants `dashboards:read`) is denied at line 117 before any permission lookup, so image rendering of that dashboard fails until the entry expires; the same cross-identity confusion applies between anonymous and a user whose UID parses to the same string.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A cached deny for one identity type is served for a different identity type that shares the same UID string, producing an incorrect PermissionDenied result.
raw_findings.impact: The render service (which `getRendererPermissions` always grants `dashboards:read`) is denied at line 117 before any permission lookup, so image rendering of that dashboard fails until the entry expires; the same cross-identity confusion applies between anonymous and a user whose UID parses to the same string.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new denial cache key is built only from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent, dropping the identity type that the existing permission cache keys encode.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Include `checkReq.IdentityType` in the denial key (e.g. add an idType component to `userPermDenialCacheKey`, mirroring how `anonymousPermCacheKey` separates anonymous from user permission keys).
raw_findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, colliding across anonymous/render/user subjects
raw_findings.trigger: An anonymous request (`subject: "anonymous:0"`) is denied `dashboards:read` on `dash1`, caching the denial under key `<ns>.perm_0_dashboards:read_dash1_`; within the 30s TTL the render service (`subject: "render:0"`, also UserUID "0") issues the same Check.

raw_findings.body: A cached denial for one (resource, folder) pair is returned for a different (resource, folder) pair the user is actually allowed to access, so the second resource is wrongly denied for the cache TTL.
raw_findings.evidence: return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent
raw_findings.failure_mode: Distinct authorization questions collapse onto one cache entry, so a deny leaks to an unrelated resource check.
raw_findings.impact: A cached denial for one (resource, folder) pair is returned for a different (resource, folder) pair the user is actually allowed to access, so the second resource is wrongly denied for the cache TTL.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new key builder joins user-controlled name and parent values with the same '_' delimiter that may occur inside those values.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use an unambiguous separator/encoding for the variable-length components (e.g. length-prefix or a character disallowed in UIDs such as '/' plus a distinct ".deny_" prefix instead of reusing ".perm_").
raw_findings.title: Denial cache key concatenation is ambiguous for UIDs containing underscores
raw_findings.trigger: Grafana UIDs allow underscores, so Check(name="a_b", folder="c") and Check(name="a", folder="b_c") for the same user/action produce the identical key `<ns>.perm_<uid>_<action>_a_b_c`.

raw_findings.body: The `iam_authz_direct_db_service_permission_cache_usage{cache_hit="true"}` counter is incremented although the permission cache was never consulted, so dashboards/alerts on permission-cache hit rate over-report hits and cannot distinguish the new denial cache.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Observability data becomes misleading; the permission cache hit ratio is inflated by unrelated denial-cache hits.
raw_findings.impact: The `iam_authz_direct_db_service_permission_cache_usage{cache_hit="true"}` counter is incremented although the permission cache was never consulted, so dashboards/alerts on permission-cache hit rate over-report hits and cannot distinguish the new denial cache.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly added denial-cache fast path reuses the existing permission-cache metric without distinguishing the cache it hit.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Emit a separate metric (or an extra label value such as `cache="denial"`) for denial-cache hits instead of reusing `permissionCacheUsage` with `cache_hit="true"`.
raw_findings.title: Denial-cache hit is counted as a permission cache hit
raw_findings.trigger: Any Check request that is short-circuited by the new `permDenialCache` lookup at line 117.

raw_findings.body: The test still passes because `scopeMap["dashboards:uid:dash1"]` is `false` (a deny) and the fake store has no permissions, so it never proves the denial cache is consulted first; the comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" contradicts the seeded value.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A regression that deletes or bypasses the denial-cache lookup would not be detected by this test.
raw_findings.impact: The test still passes because `scopeMap["dashboards:uid:dash1"]` is `false` (a deny) and the fake store has no permissions, so it never proves the denial cache is consulted first; the comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" contradicts the seeded value.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new test seeds the permission cache with a false value while intending to seed an allowing permission, removing the discriminating condition.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Seed the permission cache with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}` (an actual grant) so the assertion `assert.False(t, resp.Allowed)` only holds when the denial cache short-circuits.
raw_findings.title: Denial-cache test cannot fail: permCache is seeded with a deny value, not an allow
raw_findings.trigger: Run `TestService_CacheCheck/Should_deny_on_explicit_cache_deny_entry` with the `permDenialCache` short-circuit in `Check` removed.

raw_findings.impact: A regression in the denial-write path (wrong key, missing Set, or setting on allow) ships undetected, so the DB requery protection this PR adds is unverified.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new denial-cache population branch was added without accompanying test coverage.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a subtest that issues a denied Check against a fake store, asserts `s.permDenialCache.Get(ctx, userPermDenialCacheKey(...))` returns ok, and asserts a repeated Check does not increase `fakeStore.calls`.
raw_findings.title: No test covers writing the denial cache after a database-backed deny
raw_findings.trigger: The new `TestService_CacheCheck` subtests only pre-seed `permDenialCache`; none performs a Check that is denied via the store and then verifies the entry was written / that a subsequent Check avoids the store.

finding.trigger: An anonymous request (`subject: "anonymous:0"`) is denied `dashboards:read` on `dash1`, caching the denial under key `<ns>.perm_0_dashboards:read_dash1_`; within the 30s TTL the render service (`subject: "render:0"`, also UserUID "0") issues the same Check.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that identity type is missing from the denial cache key is correct, but the trigger scenario is unrealistic. The render service (TypeRenderService) returns permissions directly from getRendererPermissions() without hitting the denial cache path - it returns map[string]bool{"*": true} for dashboards:read. Anonymous users go through getAnonymousPermissions() which also has a separate code path. The validateSubject() function extracts both userUID and identityType, and different identity types would have different userUID values in practice (anonymous:0 vs render:0 vs user:abc123). The collision scenario requires same namespace+userUID+action+name+parent across different identity types, which is not demonstrated to be realistic.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 118 in the patch shows `s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("true", checkReq.Action).Inc()` is called when the denial cache hits, but this metric is named `permission_cache_usage` and is intended for the permission cache. The denial cache is a separate cache (permDenialCache vs permCache), so incrementing the permission cache hit metric for denial cache hits conflates two different caches in observability data.

validated_findings.body: The test still passes because `scopeMap["dashboards:uid:dash1"]` is `false` (a deny) and the fake store has no permissions, so it never proves the denial cache is consulted first; the comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" contradicts the seeded value.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A regression that deletes or bypasses the denial-cache lookup would not be detected by this test.
validated_findings.impact: The test still passes because `scopeMap["dashboards:uid:dash1"]` is `false` (a deny) and the fake store has no permissions, so it never proves the denial cache is consulted first; the comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" contradicts the seeded value.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new test seeds the permission cache with a false value while intending to seed an allowing permission, removing the discriminating condition.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Seed the permission cache with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}` (an actual grant) so the assertion `assert.False(t, resp.Allowed)` only holds when the denial cache short-circuits.
validated_findings.title: Denial-cache test cannot fail: permCache is seeded with a deny value, not an allow
validated_findings.trigger: Run `TestService_CacheCheck/Should_deny_on_explicit_cache_deny_entry` with the `permDenialCache` short-circuit in `Check` removed.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 982 shows `s.permCache.Set(ctx, userPermCacheKey("org-12", "test-uid", "dashboards:read"), map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false})` seeds the permission cache with `false` (a deny), while the comment on line 981 says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked". The test asserts `assert.False(t, resp.Allowed)` which would pass regardless of whether the denial cache is consulted, since both caches would deny. The test cannot detect if the denial cache lookup is removed.

validated_findings.body: A regression in the denial-write path (wrong key, missing Set, or setting on allow) ships undetected, so the DB requery protection this PR adds is unverified.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Untested new branch: incorrect denial-key construction or a missing Set would not fail the suite.
validated_findings.impact: A regression in the denial-write path (wrong key, missing Set, or setting on allow) ships undetected, so the DB requery protection this PR adds is unverified.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new denial-cache population branch was added without accompanying test coverage.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a subtest that issues a denied Check against a fake store, asserts `s.permDenialCache.Get(ctx, userPermDenialCacheKey(...))` returns ok, and asserts a repeated Check does not increase `fakeStore.calls`.
validated_findings.title: No test covers writing the denial cache after a database-backed deny
validated_findings.trigger: The new `TestService_CacheCheck` subtests only pre-seed `permDenialCache`; none performs a Check that is denied via the store and then verifies the entry was written / that a subsequent Check avoids the store.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap claim, not a bug in the patch. The patch adds denial cache write at line 154, and while additional test coverage would be beneficial, absence of a specific test is not a defect introduced by the patch. The existing test at line 979 does exercise the denial cache read path, demonstrating the feature works.

validated_findings.body: The `cacheHit` struct field and both `if tc.cacheHit` branches (the permCache seeding and the `require.Equal(t, 1, store.calls)` assertion) are now unreachable dead code that misleads readers into thinking the cached path is still exercised here.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability: dead test scaffolding implies coverage that no longer exists.
validated_findings.impact: The `cacheHit` struct field and both `if tc.cacheHit` branches (the permCache seeding and the `require.Equal(t, 1, store.calls)` assertion) are now unreachable dead code that misleads readers into thinking the cached path is still exercised here.
validated_findings.root_cause: The test case was removed when the cache read moved out of `getUserPermissions`, but the table field and conditional branches it drove were not cleaned up.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Drop the now-unused `cacheHit` field and its two branches from `TestService_getUserPermissions`, since the cached path is covered by `getCachedIdentityPermissions`/`TestService_CacheCheck`.
validated_findings.title: Dead `cacheHit` test dimension left behind in TestService_getUserPermissions
validated_findings.trigger: After deleting the only case with `cacheHit: true`, every remaining case sets `cacheHit: false`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The candidate claims dead code on the LEFT side (line 342), but the patch shows this test case was REMOVED (lines L342-L349 are deleted). The remaining test cases still use the cacheHit field (line 347 shows cacheHit:false, line 355 shows cacheHit:false). The field is not dead code - it's still used by remaining test cases. The claim that all remaining cases set cacheHit:false is accurate but this is intentional after removing the cache-hit test case.

validated_findings.body: All three methods (`Get`, `Set`, `Delete`) carry a `lc` receiver copied from a local-cache implementation, so the receiver name no longer relates to the type and violates the Go convention of a short receiver derived from the type name.
validated_findings.evidence: func (lc *NoopCache) Get(ctx context.Context, key string) ([]byte, error) {
validated_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability: misleading identifier suggests the type is a local cache implementation.
validated_findings.impact: All three methods (`Get`, `Set`, `Delete`) carry a `lc` receiver copied from a local-cache implementation, so the receiver name no longer relates to the type and violates the Go convention of a short receiver derived from the type name.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new no-op cache type was created by copying a local-cache implementation without renaming its receiver.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the receiver on all three `NoopCache` methods to `c` (or `n`).
validated_findings.title: NoopCache methods use receiver name `lc` inconsistent with the type
validated_findings.trigger: Reading or extending the new `NoopCache` implementation in pkg/services/authz/rbac.go.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is explicitly categorized as a style issue (receiver naming convention). The instructions state to drop stylistic claims. The receiver name `lc` vs `c` or `n` has no functional impact.
